meaningMnemonic: See the rolling hills with the road going off into the background to another hill? That's why this is the hills radical.
This looks a bit like a waiter walking toward you with a platter in their hands... but wait. It's only half of a waiter. It's a one sided waiter!
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means oversee .

This kind of looks like big ( 大 ), which I think you'll remember you learned by pretending this was a big guy. This big guy, however, has a funny leg... a peg leg. That makes him a pirate . Also, his arms are in the "YARRRR" position.

Poor turtles. We don't like them here. This is a turtle shell . See the shell with just a tail remaining? It's the only thing we didn't remove off the turtle. It's just a shell with a tail, so basically it's just a turtle shell.

A demon on a jet is pretty alluring . Demons themselves are pretty intriguing, but put one on a jet? Now that’s alluring. Hints See this demon flying around in his jet. Do you feel allured? You should. Hear the roar of the jet engine as the demon cackles.
readingMnemonic: This alluring demon on a jet wants one thing and one thing only. Me at ( み ). Human meat. This demon needs human meat to survive so he is taking his jet into the city to feast on some meat. Hints The demon won’t be so alluring once you see him scarfing down humans, tearing the meat from their bones. How gross.

meaningMnemonic: You fly north to the moon and break your back when you finally land on it. You weren’t braced for impact so when you hit the moon, your back took all of the impact. Hints Imagine flying north to the moon. Feel the force of being rocketed through space on your journey. Now feel your spine telescope and your back break. It really hurts.
readingMnemonic: Your back hurts so much that the only way to properly explain the pain is in hai ku ( はい ) form. I flew to the moon. It is there I broke my back. My back hurts real bad. Hints Say this haiku out loud. Memorize it and use this haiku to remember this kanji.

meaningMnemonic: A horse gets trapped in a small room with a stool and an insect , and together they create a very boisterous situation. The horse and the insect are both scrambling frantically to get out of the small room, knocking the stool around all over the place. Hints Imagine the boisterous sounds coming from this small room. Hear the horse neigh and stomp his hooves, hear the insect buzzing loudly, and hear the wooden stool rattle around as the horse and insect try to escape the room.
readingMnemonic: At the height of their boisterous sounds, there's a sudden, awful CRONCH(!) and you see the sou l ( そう ) of the insect slowly rising out of the room, through the ceiling. Hints The horse gets even more frightened now that it killed the insect and saw an actual soul float by its head and it grows even more boisterous.

meaningMnemonic: When you eat you want to see the shape of your gun from under a towel , so you decorate your house with them. Hints Just picture it: an entire home decorated top to bottom with guns covered in towels, so only the outline shows. As your guests try to eat you say, "Guess what gun this is?! Haha, you got it wrong, pull the towel back."
readingMnemonic: If you actually decorate your house like this it will give people quite a shock ( しょく ). In fact, they might be so shocked they run out of there screaming. Hints Maybe you should be more conscious of other people when you decorate. Or at least, don't shock people into fainting or yelling or leaving. Guns do that, you know?

meaningMnemonic: Beforehand , to buy a geoduck , you have to go to the bank to deposit enough money. If you don't deposit your money you won't have enough in your account to buy one! They're expensive, after all. Hints Imagine yourself depositing your money beforehand. Imagine the delicious geoduck you'll be able to buy now that the money has been deposited into your account.
readingMnemonic: You go to the bank to make the deposit , and there is a kid standing in your way playing with a yo -yo ( よ ). You try to squeeze past and he hits you in the face with the yo-yo. Now you can't even see, let alone make the deposit. Hints Imagine trying to make a deposit to your bank after getting hit in the face with a yo-yo. You can hardly see what you're shoving your money into. Just hope it isn't the hands of the kid that hit you.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami hits the sun , where you're in prison with a spoon trying to catch some of it before it starts to dry up . Being in prison on the sun means your thirst is truly great, and this spoon will help you quench it when the tsunami comes. Hints Imagine the feeling of drinking spoon after spoon of refreshing tsunami water, how it replenishes your dried up body. You've been in this sun prison for so long, holding onto this spoon and waiting for this moment. Better take advantage of it — even a tsunami will dry up real quick on the sun.
readingMnemonic: This method of quenching your thirst reminds you of being in a ca r wa sh ( かわ ). The water pours over you in waves, and you're stuck inside a metal cage. Totally the same thing as a car wash, right? Hints Imagine quenching your thirst in a real car wash. Open your mouth and let the soapy water dump on over and in you. You'll never be thirsty again!

meaningMnemonic: If you're a one-sided paper anti (someone against one-sided paper), then you should bind all those one-sided papers into an edition . Hints One-sided paper is just anti-everything. It's bad for the environment. It's bad for easy reading. Put all those one-sided papers together into one, big edition instead.
readingMnemonic: The first edition you create is a fan fiction all about the adventures of Han ( はん ) Solo. You hated how short and one-sided his story in Star Wars seemed to be, and trying to keep track of it all was really hard. But not anymore! Hints Please read my super special Han Solo edition of the Star Wars story. I ripped out all the one-sided pages that had him in it and put them into a single edition together so it's just the good stuff now.

meaningMnemonic: You've made yourself a tree bookshelf (that is, a bookshelf cut into a tree), so you build a fence to keep the riffraff out. Hints Your tree bookshelf is often being raided by the neighbors, and since it's outside, all you can do is build a fence around it to protect it. Better check out that fence-building book in your tree bookshelf.
readingMnemonic: On your fence , you hang up a sack ( さく ) to accept donations. Hints People put money and books in your fence sack to keep your tree bookshelf well stocked.

meaningMnemonic: Traveling in the direction of the ocean, you take a gun and shoot a crab , then stick a flag in the beach and claim it as your own. The crab was the only thing standing in the way of you conquering the area. Now that the flag is in the ground, no one can dispute who it belongs to. Hints Look at your flag and hear it flapping in the wind. Also hear your ears ringing a bit from when you shot that crab. Look at all the bits of exploded crab strewn around the area. Yowza.
readingMnemonic: To make sure that no one removes your flag , you lock it to one of the lifeguard posts and you throw away the key ( き ). Since no one will have the key to unlock the flag, no one will be able to remove it. Hints Picture yourself locking this flag up with your key. Imagine turning the key in the lock and hearing the click when it is secured.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami knocks a cleat off a child and the shoe begins to float away in the water. This child was just out playing soccer, minding his own business, when the tsunami crashed in and knocked his cleats off his feet. Now the cleat is floating away with the tsunami. Hints Your cleat is floating away but you’re floating too. The water is really deep now, but you try and float towards your cleat to retrieve it. Imagine floating in this wet water reaching for your lost cleat.
readingMnemonic: While you float in the water, an u ni ( う ) jabs into your foot. “ Uwa aa~ ( うわ )” you cry. That uni really hurts. They’re all spikey and painful and junk. “Uwaaaa~” Hints Say “Uwaaa~” out loud a few times while you imagine an うに stabbing you as you float along with the tsunami water. What a day you’ve had.

meaningMnemonic: You run every day and soon you become a human that can go beyond the normal speed limits of man. You run and you run and you run. This training allows you to become super human. You go beyond the limits of a normal human. You become a human who can run really fast. Hints Run fast! Go beyond the limits imposed upon you by nature! Imagine yourself running faster than any human has ever run ever. Feel yourself cutting through the air, wind breaking across you as you break the sound barrier. Boom!
readingMnemonic: To solidify your ability to go beyond the abilities of other humans, you etch ( えつ ) sacred runes into your legs to preserve your running abilities. Etching these runes makes sure that your skills will never deteriorate. Hints Etch these runes into your legs. Go ahead and run a finger over your legs and pretend to etch runes into them. These runes you etch will allow you to run fast forever.

meaningMnemonic: The sun is being call ed on to boil the earth by illuminating it. Hints We don't want the earth to actually boil, but we do want some of that boiling hot sun light to illuminate all of the darkness of the universe and let us see.
readingMnemonic: The person who calls the sun asking it to illuminate the earth is the Shou gun ( しょう ). It's very specifically the Shougun's responsibility to make sure the earth is illuminated every morning. Hints Picture the Shougun calling out to the sun, asking it to illuminate our planet with its boiling hot rays. You better thank the Shougun the next time you see him for everything he does for you.

meaningMnemonic: Fire you use to light up the street needs to go in a lamp . Campfires, matches? No, none of those work. You need bright, safe lamps to keep the street nice at night. Hints Picture these lamps lining the street, with their little fires burning brightly. Nowadays we don't have real fire in them, we use electricity!
readingMnemonic: These street lamp s were first used in とう きょう . It was the most advanced city after all. And more people were out at night in とうきょう than anywhere else in Japan. So they needed lamps to light things up! Hints Picture とうきょう , not lit up by all of the electricity, signs, shops, and things that light up its streets today, but by old-fashioned fire lamps!

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami rips a flag off your house in the rain , causing a leak where it was ripped out. The rain and the tsunami combined just tore the flag right off your house. The force was so strong that it actually removed part of the wall, and now you have a leak in your home. Hints Look at this leak in your house and see the rain water coming in. Hear it drip drip dripping down the wall.
readingMnemonic: The leak is getting worse and worse and so is the tsunami, when you see something outside. It’s a bunch of roe ( ろう ) floating in the waves. Using your quick thinking skills you scoop it up and shove it into the cracks where the water is leaking in. It works like a charm! Hints Did you know that roe can plug any leak? It’s true. If you don’t mind wasting some, you should break a leak into your own house and then try to plug it back up again with some salmon roe.

meaningMnemonic: A servant holding a gun sits on the ground to see if he can find something to look at . The servant is on watch duty and has the gun to protect the perimeter. He patrols the grounds to look at the distance to see if there are any trespassers. Hints Look at this servant. He’s doing a great job. Oops, looks like he sees you. Yup, he’s pointing his gun at you. Imagine staring down the barrel of his gun as you slowly back away.
readingMnemonic: You start backing away, but then you realize that you are Macho Man Ran dy ( らん ) Savage. Randy Savage backs away from no fight! I mean, look at this guy – this servant guy. Take away the gun and he’s not much to look at. You can take him. Hints Pretend you are Macho Man Randy Savage. Run at this servant guy, take his gun away, and beat him up. Ohhh yeaaahhh!

meaningMnemonic: You meet a woman from another clan under the rising sun to prepare for marriage . Your clan and her clan are standing together as the two of you watch the sun rise together. Hints Marriage is a big deal and it's going to connect your two clans, so you have to do the ceremony in the sun in front of everyone so they can see.
readingMnemonic: For the marriage to be official, you need to wait for a con dor ( こん ) to appear. If it doesn't show up before the sun goes down again, the marriage was a failure. You have to try again tomorrow with a different woman. Hints Do you want to go through with this marriage? You better hope you see a condor then! It's the official bird of love and unification, ya know. That's why so many people wait until they're older to get married these days, because there aren't as many condors thanks to deforestation.

meaningMnemonic: Who is this woman mole ?! It's your niece ! Hints Who else would it be but your niece? In fact, all of your nieces are actually moles! Picture what your family gatherings would look like with all those mole-nieces. Quite terrifying, really…
readingMnemonic: Not only are they moles, all of your niece s were also born in May ( めい )! Hints Picture your many nieces, all moles, and all born in the same month of May. Every year, like clockwork, a new mole-niece is born into your family in May.

meaningMnemonic: A piece of your soul lives in a cross that you keep in a net -like pocket inside your clothing because of the nostalgia it brings you. Someone special gave you that cross, and you feel great nostalgia when you look at it. That's why you keep it in your bosom pocket , close to your heart. Hints Try to imagine the person who gave you this nostalgic cross. Was it a grandparent? An old friend or mentor, perhaps? Reach into your bosom pocket and think back on those good old days.
readingMnemonic: The nostalgia hits you the hardest in 夏 ( なつ ). It was a beautiful 夏 day many years ago when you were given that cross that you keep in your bosom pocket . Hints Put on your rosy-tinted glasses and bask in the nostalgic memories of 夏 days long past.

meaningMnemonic: Point some fingers at the sun and put some others in your ear as you sit on a stool — now you can have your photograph taken. This is a glamour photo , so you have to be in one of these weird, artsy poses for it to come out juuust right. Hints Which fingers do you point at the sun, and which do you put in your ear? Act it out, that'll help you remember. Now try to relax on the stool and smile for the camera. This is a professional photograph, so you better do what you're told!
readingMnemonic: As you're getting the photograph taken, the photographer tells you to say Satsu ki ( さつ ). He says it's like saying cheese but more effective. Satsuki! Hints Go ahead and say Satsuki out loud, all happy-like. Makes a pretty big smile, right? From now on you should always say Satsuki when you're being photographed.

meaningMnemonic: The tree pirate jumps from a tree and attacks you by hitting you with a pillow . Hints It hurts a little bit, but the fact that tree pirates use pillows as their weapons is a bit anticlimactic.
readingMnemonic: As he hits you with his pillow he makes a demand: "Give me your Mac cooler ( まくら ). He wants the device that cools down your Mac computer. Hints You give him your Mac cooler and he goes on his way. He's quite happy he can cool down his Mac, now. The trees are quite warm and he hears this will help to cool down his tree apples.

meaningMnemonic: On a scooter running in one direction is a gun -toting child . This is a terribly dangerous situation, but to the child it is just play . Hints Imagine a child riding a scooter with a gun having a good time. "Come play with me!" they shout. "No!" you yell back.
readingMnemonic: Everything is play for you ths ( ゆう ), even if it's a terrible, scary, not good situation like this one. Hints Imagine trying to explain to the youth that this is not play and that they should stop, but them youths can't stop playing. P.S. From the WaniKani staff to you: Don't let youths play with guns, please.

meaningMnemonic: The soul of a person has a hook that can make them pleasant . When you see, hear, or feel something pleasant, can't you feel that hook pressing into the middle of your body? Hints Imagine that feeling you get when everything is just SO pleasant. There is a pressure from your soul's hook digging in. It's a good feeling though, a pleasant one! It isn't too hard or too soft.
readingMnemonic: If you want to feel this pleasant feeling just look at a kay ak ( かい ). Kayaks are the most pleasant boats in the world. Feel that pleasant feeling in your chest just from reading about kayaks in this mnemonic right now. Hints Go look up pictures of kayaks to get some of that pleasant high. Mm, your soul is hooking you real good.

meaningMnemonic: Those that can only eat a part of a shellfish are probably a bit poor . Hints Poor people can't even afford a whole shellfish. They have to settle with just a part.
readingMnemonic: And since they are poor , they are getting these shellfish parts from the trash bin ( びん ). It's quite unfortunate. Hints Imagine a poor person going through a garbage bin to find only a part of of a shellfish. What a sad sight.

meaningMnemonic: If you do yoga correct ly, you will not only prolong your body but your life! Hints Do you want to prolong your life? Then do yoga correctly!
readingMnemonic: You can prolong your life with correct yoga techniques, but unfortunately, if you ever stop doing yoga after you've started this prolonging process, it will just en d ( えん ) suddenly. Hints Correct yoga will prolong your life but no yoga will end it. Do you think that's a fair trade?

meaningMnemonic: You give a shellfish to a lifeguard to purchase their services. You think lifeguards are interested in normal money? Come on, they're obviously out there using shellfish for their purchases. It's only natural, given their seaside habitat. Hints Imagine the grooved surface of a shellfish shell as you press it into the hand of a lifeguard. Congrats, you've just completed a purchase. Uh… what'd you get?
readingMnemonic: This time you purchase some こう いち goods. You know, since you're such a fan. How else can you show love in this world, if not through purchases? The lifeguard hands over a little haul of こういち plushies and figurines. Nice. Hints And it's totally because those こういち goods are so valuable that the lifeguard accepts shellfish for them. Has nothing to do with the fact he couldn't get real money for them, okay? Hint: When you see the "lifeguard" radical, the reading is probably going to be こう .

meaningMnemonic: Take your fingers , put them on this turtle shell , and push push push! Push the turtle right on out of there. Hints Picture yourself using your fingers to push a turtle out of its shell. It really doesn't want to leave, so you have to push really hard.
readingMnemonic: You're trying to push this turtle out so you can use the shell for your new o bi ( お ). You keep seeing other people wearing turtle shell patterns on their obi, but you're going to go a step further. You're going to MAKE your obi out of actual turtle shells! You just have to push this darn turtle out first. Hints Imagine pushing some turtle shells flat to make a beautiful obi. Wear it out, watch everyone gasp in awe. Oh... oh no! They're trying to push you out of your obi like you did the turtle. They're mad about your turtle crime!

meaningMnemonic: If you look for a leaf among the hills you will notice they are scarce . The hills have no trees around them, so there are no leaves. The leaves are scarce here on the hills. Hints Imagine being on the hills. You want a leaf to find and take back as a souvenir but there are none. Imagine looking feverishly for a leaf even though you don’t really expect to find one.
readingMnemonic: Still looking for a leaf, you determine that they are far too scarce to find here. Just before you give up, you discover a giant bow ling ( ぼう ) ball. As you pick it up, another one comes thundering down the hill knocking over a tiny tree. Hints Leaves are scarce here because someone is using these hills for their bowling. The bowling balls knock over everything, and leaves can't grow.

meaningMnemonic: You're stuck in prison with nothing but a spoon , and the smell in here is so bad you’re using the prison spoon to waft it outside as best you can. Hints It smells awful in this prison. You have to act fast with your prison spoon to get rid of all the bad smells!
readingMnemonic: You can’t believe how awful these smell s are. You’re new in prison, so you call them all neo -smells ( にお ). They're neo, they're new to you. Hints Try to come up with some neo-smells right now. There’s the neo-food smell (prison cafeteria pizza, maybe) and the neo-laundry smell of course (your prison uniform). Can you think of any other neo-smells?

meaningMnemonic: The next plate is the one you will steal . This one would be too obvious, better wait for the next one. Hints Wait for this next plate. Here it is—now steal it! Imagine stealing this plate and making off with it.
readingMnemonic: You steal this plate from a とう きょう restaurant, so after you steal it, picture yourself running through the streets of とうきょう as you lose your pursuers. Hints Be careful not to drop that plate! Wouldn’t want to steal something just to break it. Imagine running through the streets of とうきょう . See all the sights and hear all the sounds. Just don’t get too distracted, you gotta get to a safe place and stash your stolen plate away.

meaningMnemonic: A scooter with a mohawk , now that's the most suitable hairstyle you could ever think of for a scooter! Hints You keep seeing scooters all over the city with mohawks and you can't get it out of your head that it's the most suitable thing you've ever seen.
readingMnemonic: You want this suitable hairstyle for your scooter too, and luckily you're a techie ( てき ), so it's easy for you to install one. Hints Imagine going online to check out some of your techie message boards and learning the most suitable mohawk for your scooter then installing it yourself.

meaningMnemonic: Whenever all the feathers start stand ing, you know it's time for the next day. Once the day comes to its end, all feathers start standing up like clockwork. Hints Imagine every single feather simultaneously standing up once the next day gets closer. It's like some kind of ritual that's repeated at the end of every single day. Must be stressful to be a feathered animal!
readingMnemonic: With the next day approaching and all feathers standing up, you get ready to drink your usual liter of yolk ( よく ). Yes, you heard that right. Hints Imagine having to drink an entire liter of egg yolk at the end of each day. Just like the feathers have their ritual of standing up, you have your own ritual of downing a liter of egg yolk. Just don't ask questions.

meaningMnemonic: You take some bamboo and attach it together into a token of appreciation for your friend. Your friend greatly appreciates this token of friendship. Hints Imagine trying to attach some bamboo together into a token for someone.
readingMnemonic: You hand over the token but your friend drops it and yells, "You foo l ( ふ )! I'm allergic to bamboo!" Hints Imagine the embarrassment you feel, forgetting they were allergic to bamboo. Oh well, it’s the thought that counts. You’re still a fool, though.

meaningMnemonic: If a tsunami hits, it's rain ing, and you're outside trying to use a rake , you're going to be very wet and damp . Hints Imagine how wet and damp you'd be with tsunami water up to your knees and rain pouring down on your head. You struggle with your rake anyway.
readingMnemonic: You can't stand how wet and damp you feel in these clothes so you rip them off and rake in the nu de ( ぬ )! Hints You're still wet, but at least you don't have the feeling of damp clothes touching your body now. You'll have to be really careful raking in the nude though.

meaningMnemonic: With just one look at something you're able to take in all the info you need, because that something is a list . A nice list that gives you an overview at a glance. Perfect for all that looking over you have to do. You busy consumer of information, you. 一覧 usually refers to a neat list you can skim over easily to get the info you need, like a guest list or a data table. With する , it becomes a pretty formal verb for looking over something in a quick way, like skimming through a report or casually checking out a place.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 覚えたい日本語の単語の一覧を作りました。
sentences.english: I made a list of Japanese words that I want to memorize.

sentences.japanese: アフリカの歴史書をまとめて一覧できるようにしてみました。
sentences.english: I've compiled a list of books on African history for easy reference.

sentences.japanese: このキーとこのキーを同時に押したら、キーボードショートカットの一覧が出てくるよ。
sentences.english: If you press this key and this key at the same time, a list of keyboard shortcuts will appear.

sentences.japanese: 連絡先の一覧から中々上司の名前が見つからないんだけど。
sentences.english: I'm struggling to find my boss's name on my contact list.

meaningMnemonic: The previous extent of time was a little while ago . Just think to a previous extent of time that was indeed a little while ago. Now, associate! 先程 is limited to a relatively brief time frame within the same day. So it can be used for something mentioned earlier in a speech or at an event from earlier in the day , but not for something from a few days ago. 先程 is also polite and formal, so it's generally used in professional or respectful settings.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the words 先 and 程 , put together.

sentences.japanese: あれ、先程コンビニでもお会いしましたよね？
sentences.english: Oh, we met earlier at the convenience store too, didn't we?

sentences.japanese: 先程からあそこに座っているご老人はだれですか。
sentences.english: Who is the old man sitting over there from a little while ago?

sentences.japanese: 先程も申しましたように、お客様の予約はキャンセルされました。
sentences.english: As I told you earlier, your reservation was cancelled.

sentences.japanese: 先程あなたからの手紙を読ませて頂きました。
sentences.english: I read the letter from you earlier today.

meaningMnemonic: The alluring power is the power of allure .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 彼女の魅力を一言で表すのは難しい。
sentences.english: It's hard to describe her charm in just one word.

sentences.japanese: このレストランは安さと量が魅力です。味もなかなかですよ。
sentences.english: The appeal of this restaurant lies in its affordability and generous portions. The taste is also quite good.

sentences.japanese: 都会の魅力といえば、やはり便利さと刺激的な生活ですね。
sentences.english: The appeal of city life is definitely its convenience and exciting lifestyle.

sentences.japanese: 私はゴルフの魅力に取り憑かれてしまいました。
sentences.english: I became obsessed with the charm of golf.

meaningMnemonic: The play park ground is where you go play. It's fun. It's an amusement park !
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: この遊園地はデートスポットとして人気があります。
sentences.english: This amusement park is popular as a dating spot.

sentences.japanese: 遊園地のフードコートでたこ焼きを食べました。
sentences.english: I ate takoyaki at the amusement park food court.

sentences.japanese: あの神戸の遊園地は、小さい子と遊びに行くにはいい所ですよ。
sentences.english: That amusement park in Kobe is a nice place to go and play with little kids.

sentences.japanese: 「スカイダイビングをして、その後遊園地に行くんだけど、一緒に行かない？」「えーっ、絶対に嫌！」
sentences.english: "I am going to go skydiving then afterwards go to a theme park. You want to join me?" "What? Absolutely not!"

meaningMnemonic: Everything is suitable and right . Therefore it is appropriate , proper , and suitable . Strangely enough, this also means irresponsible . Maybe it's because when everything is suitable and right for you, you're taking too much and not leaving enough for everyone else, making you irresponsible?
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 適当な答えを選んでください。
sentences.english: Please choose the appropriate answer.

sentences.japanese: あいつは適当な事ばかり言っている。
sentences.english: That guy often says irresponsible things.

sentences.japanese: 居酒屋で、同僚が店員に「適当にお願いします」と言って注文をしたことに驚きました。
sentences.english: I was surprised when my colleague was ordering in an izakaya and said to the waitress: "Choose whatever you think is best".

meaningMnemonic: The clothes with which I decorate myself with is my attire or my fashion .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 私は服飾専門学校を卒業しました。
sentences.english: I graduated from a fashion technical school.

sentences.japanese: 今の服飾の仕事は、遊び半分でしてるんですよ。
sentences.english: I'm working in the clothing business now, mostly for fun.

meaningMnemonic: ご覧 is the polite noun form of 見る and means looking at , seeing , or watching . Some other common phrases you might hear are ご覧ください (please take a look) or ご覧のとおり (as you can see). They're formal but common in polite speech, such as in customer service or business presentations. ご覧 can even be used on its own as a gentle command, like ほら、そこをご覧 ("Hey, look over there").

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. Remember how 詰める means "to stuff in"? Well, this is the intransitive version that focuses on the thing being stuffed, so it means to be stuffed with or to be crammed full . You can remember this because your pillow is stuffed with まる the cat's hair. It's filled almost to bursting with bits of まる , making it extremely soft and comfy. Like your まる -stuffed pillow, 詰まる is used when something completely fills up a space, whether it's a wallet packed with bills (you wish), a book filled with tons of useful information, or a schedule full of to-dos. It can also mean to be stuck or to be clogged , so you can use it if something gets stuck in your throat, or even when your toilet is clogged.

meaningMnemonic: You learned that 垂れる means "to droop" or "to drip." Well, this is the transitive version of that, meaning it takes a direct object. This time, you're the one making something droop or drip, which is why this word means to dangle something or to dribble something . You can remember it's transitive because of the す ending, which you've seen with lots of transitive verbs by now. 垂らす describes when you dangle something or let something hang in a way which allows gravity to act on it, like hanging a line when fishing. It's also used to describe letting something drip — for example, a little kid letting mucus drip from their nose or a sleeping person dribbling drool out of their mouth.

meaningMnemonic: A float ing world painting is what you call an ukiyo-e woodblock print in Japan. The "floating world" refers to an evanescent world that is impermanent (floating), just as beauty and entertainment are. Back in the day, this type of art was made into woodblock prints and paintings. Unfortunately, we don't have a name for these in English because they're so unique and special, but they come up more than you'd think, so get used to ukiyo-e!

Take a look at the word and break everything down. 浮 takes the kun'yomi うき (from 浮く ), 世 also takes the kun'yomi よ , and then 絵 takes the on'yomi え . Put that all together and you have うきよえ ! Or if you already know the word ukiyo-e, that works too!

sentences.english: Every joint in my body is throbbing somehow.

sentences.japanese: あの人、言葉の節々にトゲがあるよね。
sentences.english: That person makes some harsh word choices, huh?

sentences.japanese: 早織は節々の痛みを感じて目を覚ました。

meaningMnemonic: If you view and look at something, you are viewing that thing, or watching it.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 観覧席はもう満席になりました。
sentences.english: The viewing seats are already full.

sentences.japanese: 観覧中は写真撮影が禁止されています。
sentences.english: Photography is prohibited during the viewing.

sentences.japanese: ちゃんと投げろ！遊び球を投げるところを観覧しに来たんじゃないぞ！
sentences.english: Throw it properly! I didn't come to see you throw a practice ball!

sentences.japanese: トーフグテレビの撮影現場を観覧しました。
sentences.english: I watched the TofuguTV filming.

meaningMnemonic: A leak of water is a water leakage .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 漏水の原因は古くなったパイプでした。
sentences.english: The cause of the water leak was an old pipe.

sentences.japanese: 漏水してるかもって管理会社に電話したら、すぐに来てくれたよ！
sentences.english: I called the management company about a possible water leak, and they came right away!

sentences.japanese: 漏水が原因で電気系統にトラブルが起きることもあります。
sentences.english: Water leakage can cause issues with electrical systems.

meaningMnemonic: You put one cup of liquid ... no, one full cup of liquid spirit into what you're doing. None of this half-cup garbage. A full one. That means you're going at it with all one's might .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help if you've seen 一杯 before.

sentences.japanese: チームのために精一杯努力します。
sentences.english: I will do my best for the team.

sentences.japanese: 彼は精一杯のプレゼンをしました。
sentences.english: He gave the presentation with all his effort.

sentences.japanese: 八月三十日午後五時の締切まで、精一杯頑張りました。
sentences.english: I tried my best until the deadline at 5 p.m. on August 30th.

sentences.japanese: 今は古い写真を捨てることが私にできる精一杯です。
sentences.english: Getting rid of old pictures is the best I can do for now.
